# Incident Report — MTA Exercise 2022-01-07 PCAP Analysis

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **192.168.1.216** | Dominant flow endpoint, source of all attacker traffic |
| MAC address | **9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9** | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==192.168.1.216`), matches DHCP client MAC and `eth.src` on all frames from .216 |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (also broadcast as NetBIOS `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2`/`SPOONWATCH`) | DHCP option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2`; NBNS `<00>` workstation name from 192.168.1.216; DNS queries for `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2.local`, domain `spoonwatch.net` |
| Logged-in user | **steve.smith** | Kerberos `CNameString` from 192.168.1.216 to the DC (192.168.1.2, `SPOONWATCH-DC`), authenticating as `steve.smith` alongside the machine account `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$` |

The domain controller is `192.168.1.2` (`SPOONWATCH-DC.spoonwatch.net`, MAC `20:47:47:62:ae:26`) — LAN gateway is `192.168.1.1` (MAC `1c:17:d3:f6:df:0a`).

## Malware Family — Attribution: Behavioral

No IDS/Suricata alert file was present in the evidence directory (only the pcap and pre-exported HTTP objects), so this is **not signature-confirmed**. Behavioral fingerprint from the traffic and recovered files:

- Info-stealer style exfiltration ZIP (`_5861695120.zip`, SHA256 `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f`) uploaded to the C2, containing the folder layout `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/`, plus `passwords.txt`, `system.txt`, `outlook.txt`, `screenshot.jpg` — this is the standard log structure produced by commodity browser-credential stealers (RedLine/Vidar/Raccoon-class malware).
- Prior to exfiltration, the host pulled seven auxiliary PE **DLL** modules from the same C2, each disguised with a `.jpg` extension and served with `Content-Type: image/jpeg` despite an `MZ`/`PE` header. Two of them statically link `sqlite3.dll` and Mozilla's `nss3.dll` — the exact combination used by stealers to read Chromium `Login Data`/`Web Data` SQLite databases and decrypt Firefox-stored credentials via NSS.
- Beaconing/check-in behavior: empty-body multipart `POST` requests to `/osk/`, `/osk//main.php`, sent over plain HTTP directly to a bare IP with no corresponding DNS lookup — consistent with a hardcoded C2 IP typical of stealer loaders.

**Assessed family: an information-stealer of the RedLine/Vidar-class** (browser autofill + credit-card + cookie + password harvesting with a modular DLL-loader stage). This is a behavioral judgment, not a signature match.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` (TCP) — evidence: all attacker HTTP traffic (`ip.addr==2.56.57.108`), bare-IP `Host: 2.56.57.108` header, no DNS resolution observed for this IP, first contact 2022-01-07 20:07:32 (capture-relative), 3335 frames / 3.6 MB total.

**Malicious URLs (all to 2.56.57.108, HTTP)**
- `POST http://2.56.57.108/osk/` — initial check-in
- `POST http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` — gate/exfil endpoint (carries the stolen-data ZIP as multipart form-data, field name `file`, filename `_5861695120.zip`)
- `POST http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` — module-retrieval requests (empty POST body triggers a PE/DLL download in the HTTP response body, mislabeled `image/jpeg`)

**Transferred files / hashes (SHA256, from exported HTTP objects)**
| File (as served) | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `1(1).jpg` | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` | PE32 DLL (console) — embeds SQLite3 |
| `2(1).jpg` | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` | PE32 DLL (GUI) — embeds nss3.dll |
| `3(1).jpg` | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` | PE32 DLL (GUI) |
| `4(1).jpg` | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` | PE32 DLL (console) |
| `5(1).jpg` | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` | PE32 DLL (GUI) — embeds nss3.dll, sqlite3 |
| `6(1).jpg` | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` | PE32 DLL (GUI) — embeds nss3.dll, sqlite3 |
| `7(1).jpg` | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` | PE32 DLL (console) |
| `_5861695120.zip` (exfil, extracted from POST body) | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` | Stolen-data package: browser autofill, saved credit cards, cookies, passwords, Outlook data, and a screenshot |

No malicious domain was observed — the C2 is contacted by bare IP only.

## Benign Context (not indicators)

- `2.56.57.108` had **no DNS resolution** — flagged as malicious.
- All other external endpoints are legitimate Microsoft/Windows infrastructure: `download.windowsupdate.com` / `au.download.windowsupdate.com` (23.38.189.225/.201) serving genuine Defender antimalware definition updates (`am_delta_patch_*.exe`, legitimately Microsoft-signed update channel) and `.cab` files; `ctldl.windowsupdate.com` (8.253.189.126) trusted-root CTL update; telemetry/services to `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `settings-win.data.microsoft.com`, `pti.store.microsoft.com`, `www.bing.com`, `api.msn.com` — all standard Windows 10/11 background noise.
- Internal AD/domain traffic (Kerberos, LDAP, CLDAP, DRSUAPI, SMB/SMB2 to `192.168.1.2` `SPOONWATCH-DC`) is normal domain-join activity, not malicious.

## Incident Summary

The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-GXMYNO2** (192.168.1.216, MAC 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9), logged in as domain user **steve.smith**, was compromised by an information-stealer that communicated over plain HTTP with a hardcoded C2 at **2.56.57.108:80**. The malware retrieved seven auxiliary DLL modules (disguised as `.jpg` files under `/osk/`) that bundle SQLite and Mozilla NSS libraries for reading browser-stored data, then exfiltrated a ZIP archive (`_5861695120.zip`) containing harvested Chrome/Edge autofill data, saved credit card numbers, cookies, passwords, Outlook data, and a desktop screenshot to `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php`. Attribution to a specific named family is behavioral only, based on the RedLine/Vidar-class log structure and loader pattern, since no IDS signature evidence was present in this evidence set.
